Основною ціллю була Київщина.

Ukraine Strikes Wildberries Warehouse in Russia, Putting 8th Major Logistics Hub Out of Action — A Ukrainian drone attack damaged a major Wildberries logistics center in Russia's Tula region, forcing it to suspend operations. According to independent Russian outlet Agentstvo, eight of the marketplace's 15 largest warehouses have now stopped operating following Ukrainian strikes.

NATO Membership Now Irrelevant for Ukraine? — Former Ukrainian military chief Valeriy Zaluzhnyi’s claim that NATO membership is no longer central to Ukraine’s security debate raises a deeper question: did Russia’s invasion achieve the opposite of its stated goals? Timothy Ash argues that Moscow’s war has strengthened Ukraine’s military and pushed Europe toward a historic defense buildup.

Russian Strike Triggers Ammonia Leak in Kyiv; Emergency Crews Contain Threat — A Russian missile strike damaged a specialized ammonia tank in Kyiv’s Holosiivskyi district, causing a leak during a wider overnight assault. Emergency crews contained it by 2:10 a.m., and officials said nearby residents were not at risk.

Ukraine’s Strikes Bring Blackouts, Fuel Shortages and ‘Road of Death’ to Occupied Crimea — Ukraine’s intensified strikes on occupied Crimea are disrupting fuel supplies, power infrastructure and Russian logistics. Residents face blackouts, soaring petrol prices and increasingly dangerous routes linking the peninsula to Russia.

Children’s Hospital in Zaporizhzhia Hit by Russian Strike; Children and Medics Saved by Shelter — Russian forces struck the grounds of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Children’s Clinical Hospital, damaging its facade and windows. All children and medical staff were in a shelter and survived unharmed.

Why a Chilling Video of a Kherson Vegetable Seller Has Shocked Ukraine — Footage from Kherson shows an FPV drone pursuing 52-year-old Yuriy around his vegetable truck before exploding. He survived, but the attack mirrors a wider pattern documented by the UN of civilians near the front being hunted during ordinary daily tasks.

17 Killed in Russia’s Third Kyiv Barrage in a Week Amid Critical Patriot Shortage — Russia launched another combined drone and ballistic missile assault on Kyiv, killing 15 people and injuring 22. Residential and non-residential buildings were damaged, an ambulance was hit, and an ammonia leak was contained.

Zelensky: Kyiv in ‘Daily Contact’ With Trump Team, Some Work Remains ‘Non-Public’ — Zelensky said Ukraine is in daily contact with Trump’s team and ready for meetings in any format. He expects Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to step up in August, while some diplomatic work with other partners remains “non-public.”

Ukraine Repels Russian Assaults Across 12 Frontline Axes on Tuesday — The Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) repelled Russian assaults across multiple axes on Tuesday, Aug. 4, with the Pokrovsk axis seeing 23 attacks. Russian forces carried out 216 combat clashes, fired 6,428 kamikaze drones, and dropped 213 guided bombs (KABs), according to Ukraine's General Staff.

India Declines Russia’s Offer to Purchase Su-57E Fighter Jets — India has declined Russia’s offer to purchase Su-57E stealth fighter jets, choosing instead to modernize its roughly 260-strong Su-30MKI fleet and push forward its domestically produced Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program.

Russia Lost 30,272 Troops to Ukrainian Drone Strikes in July Alone, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian drone strikes killed or badly wounded 30,272 Russian troops in July alone, based only on cases with clear video evidence. He praised Ukraine’s Security Service’s (SSU) Alpha unit for leading in successful target engagements.

New Law Grants Equal Military Rights to Ukraine’s Former Convict Soldiers — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a new law on Tuesday Aug. 4, granting former convicts serving under military contract the same rights as other soldiers, including medical care, leave, and transfer options. Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, passed the bill on July 14 with 309 votes in favor.

Zelensky Sets 3 Priorities to Speed up Ukraine’s EU Accession Bid — President Volodymyr Zelensky outlined three main priorities for accelerating Ukraine’s EU accession bid on Tuesday, Aug. 4, framing EU membership as a security matter instead of just an economic one. Two negotiation clusters have opened since mid-June, with four more in preparation.

Syria To Cut Russian Oil Imports per US Request — According to Reuters’ sources, Syria has told the US it is willing to drastically cut Russian oil imports as part of talks on removing its remaining terrorism sanctions designation. The pledge comes as Damascus seeks to diversify its energy supply.

Ozon Stops Calling Crimea Part of Russia in Support Chat — A TikTok video circulating online claims Russian e-commerce platform Ozon no longer treats occupied Crimea as part of Russia in customer support responses. Kyiv Post could not independently verify whether the response reflects an official policy or an isolated support message.

Ukraine's Economy Grows 0.6% in Q2 2026, Trails NBU's Estimate — Ukraine's economy grew 0.6% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, a flash estimate from the State Statistics Service showed, falling short of the National Bank's 0.8% calculation. The NBU said expanded budget stimulus and an improving energy grid drove the rebound, but intensified Russian strikes on ports and business infrastructure limited faster growth.

From Licensing to the First Ukrainian-Made Patriot Missile: The Road Ukraine Must Travel — As Ukraine seeks to reduce its dependence on foreign missile supplies, the prospect of licensed Patriot interceptor production has emerged as one of the country’s most ambitious defense-industrial projects. Yet obtaining a license is only the first step in a complex journey that requires advanced technology transfer, industrial infrastructure, highly skilled personnel, and long-term strategic commitment.

One Week On: Was Zelensky’s Washington Visit Really a Success? — Zelensky appears to have repaired relations with Trump and secured a strong bipartisan display in the Senate. But Washington announced no new weapons package, the sanctions bill remains unfinished, and the proposed Patriot-production agreement is still under negotiation.

Russian Airstrikes on Kramatorsk Injure 22 Civilians — At least 22 people were injured after Russia struck central Kramatorsk with two guided aerial bombs on Tuesday. The attack hit a residential apartment building, prompting an ongoing search-and-rescue operation, according to regional authorities.

New Defense Minister Hires Ukraine’s Top Audit Firm for Due Diligence on Army Contractors — Ukraine’s new defense minister, Yevhen Khmara, is using YouControl’s digital vetting tools to fight military procurement corruption. The move targets risky contractors after scandals involving the alleged $40 million in ammunition fraud and $17 million in food overpricing.

Zelensky Greenlights New SBU Operations Against Russia — President Zelensky authorized new SBU operations against Russian aggression and approved steps to remove personnel who “work for themselves, not for Ukraine.” The announcement follows a 40-day operation approved in late June.

Georgia's Only Oil Refinery to Stop Processing Russian Crude — Black Sea Petroleum LLC, owner of Georgia's only oil refinery, confirmed on Monday, Aug. 4, that it is phasing out Russian crude oil. The Kulevi refinery began processing Kazakh-origin crude in early July and expects a shipment of Libyan crude between Aug. 20-30 under an agreement running through 2027. The move follows EU sanctions that gave the refinery until January 2027 to end Russian oil processing.

Video Shows Russian FPV Drone Chasing Civilian Through Kherson Before Exploding — A Russian FPV drone was filmed chasing a civilian through a Kherson street before exploding nearby, leaving the man injured. Ukrainian officials condemned the attack as a deliberate hunt for civilians and called it another Russian war crime requiring an international response.

SBU Says Russia Using 'Honey Traps' to Assassinate Ukrainian Soldiers — On Tuesday, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) warned that Russian intelligence services have significantly intensified efforts to assassinate Ukrainian soldiers using “honey traps” – fake online dating encounters. The SBU said it has foiled more than 50 such attempts since the start of 2026.

Ukrainian Drones Strike Syzran Oil Refinery Again, Hit More Wildberries Warehouses — Drones reportedly struck Russia’s Syzran oil refinery and a Wildberries warehouse near Tver as Moscow claimed it intercepted 320 Ukrainian UAVs overnight. The refinery had only recently resumed operations following a July attack.

Russia May Target Water Supply This Winter, Kyiv Warns — Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia’s next winter campaign may focus on Ukraine’s water infrastructure after devastating attacks on the power grid. He said Kyiv is strengthening critical infrastructure while seeking additional Patriot missiles and financial support from allies.

A Letter The Economist Conveniently Ignored — The Economist was taken to task for its shameless promotion of a man who lives and thrives at Putin’s pleasure and advocates for business as usual with Moscow. Kyiv Post presents a scathing letter to the editor that the British publication decided not to publish.

Ceuta Between a Migration Crisis and a Hybrid Attack: Giorgia Meloni’s Policy and Europe’s Security — The European Democrats’ attack on Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is politically dishonest and shows that part of Europe’s center still does not understand the world in which it lives.

2 Children Killed in Russian Guided Bomb Strike on Sumy — A Russian guided bomb attack on Sumy killed three civilians, including two girls aged 5 and 10, and damaged civilian infrastructure overnight. The strike came as Moscow continues using aerial bombs to target Ukrainian cities near the border, despite growing Ukrainian electronic warfare efforts against the weapons.

Oschadbank, Ukreximbank to Sell Gulliver Mall for $207 Million Starting Price — State-owned Oschadbank and Ukreximbank will auction Kyiv’s Gulliver multifunctional complex through the Prozorro.Sales system from September, with a $207 million floor price. The banks seized the 157,000-square-meter (1.7 million-square-foot) complex from sanctioned businessman Viktor Polishchuk’s Three O LLC in July 2025 after the borrower stopped servicing its debt.

Ukraine Strikes Wildberries Hubs Near Moscow, St. Petersburg in Fresh Drone Wave — Ukraine struck two major Wildberries logistics hubs near Moscow and St. Petersburg in overnight drone attacks, extending a campaign targeting Russia’s supply network. The latest strikes reportedly damaged one of the retailer’s largest distribution centers as Ukraine continues to pressure Russia’s logistics infrastructure deep behind the front lines.

Hysteria in Russia: ‘Nowhere to Hide’ as Putin’s Palace Falls Within Ukraine’s Reach — Drone activity near Gelendzhik has turned Putin’s $1 billion Black Sea palace into a symbol of Russia’s shrinking sense of security. As Moscow decries Ukrainian strikes, Kyiv’s growing deep-strike campaign is forcing the war back toward the state that launched it.

Kyiv Under Air Raid Alert as Russian Drones Threaten Capital, Regions — Kyiv and several Ukrainian regions were placed under air raid alert overnight amid a threat from Russian attack drones. Authorities urged residents to remain in shelters.

Umerov to Lead Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence While Retaining Chief Peace Negotiator Role — Rustem Umerov will lead Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service while remaining Kyiv’s chief peace negotiator. His expanding portfolio also includes international Drone Deals, the Freyja anti-ballistic program and deeper intelligence cooperation with allies.

Russian Drone Strike Destroys Major Ukrainian Postal Hub, Hits Civilian Logistics Network — Russian forces struck Pryluky with three drones, destroying a Nova Poshta cargo branch and damaging warehouses with agricultural machinery. One man was wounded, while postal workers and customers sheltering at the site were unharmed.

Russia Jails Ukrainian for 24 Years in Case Rights Groups Call Politically Motivated — A Russian military court sentenced 30-year-old Ukrainian Yan Haupt to 24 years in prison over alleged plans to attack railway infrastructure in Krasnodar. Rights groups say the case is another politically motivated prosecution of a Ukrainian by Russian authorities.

Zaluzhny: ‘Ukraine Will Never Join NATO’ — Ukraine’s former commander-in-chief and current ambassador to the United Kingdom, Valery Zaluzhny, told a gathering of top diplomats in Kyiv that Ukraine will never become a NATO member, citing the alliance’s outdated ideologies. He urged Kyiv to instead pursue other security guarantees.

US Envoy Whitaker Says No Patriot Missile Production Deal Yet for Ukraine — US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker said Washington has not finalized any deal allowing Ukraine to produce Patriot interceptor missiles, even as talks on co-production with Ukrainian and European partners continue. He said the immediate priority is speeding up air defense deliveries before winter.

Zelensky Replacing Stefanishyna as Ukraine’s Ambassador to the US — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree on Monday, Aug. 3, removing Olha Stefanishyna as Ukraine’s ambassador to the US, ending a tenure of less than a year following corruption allegations.

4 Dead, 15 Wounded as Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces struck the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 60 times on Monday, Aug. 3, killing four people, including a child, and wounding at least 15 others. Civilian infrastructure sustained damage across four districts, according to the regional authorities.

300-Year-Old Church Destroyed By Russian Drone Strike in Kherson Region — A Russian drone strike on Sunday, Aug. 2, destroyed the nearly 300-year-old Holy Vvedenska Church in Beryslav, Kherson region. The church marked one of the region’s last remaining heritage sites, with its oak structure surviving continuous shelling since the area’s liberation in 2022.

Naftogaz Pushes €1.2 Billion in Eurobond Debt Into the 2030s — Naftogaz has restructured two Eurobond series worth approximately €1.2 billion, extending their maturities after securing approval from more than 90% of bondholders. It is the second restructuring of the debt since 2023 and comes as the company faces mounting repair costs and prepares for the 2026-27 heating season.

Russia Threatens Apple With $50M Fine Over Kremlin-Backed Messenger — Russia’s anti-monopoly agency has threatened Apple with a 4 billion rubles ($49.7 million) fine for not fully complying with its demand to remove foreign search engines by default and pre-install Kremlin-sanctioned digital services. The company previously took down one such messenger from its marketplace in June.

Italy Rejects Claim Moscow Blast Was Meant to Intimidate Italians — Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani rejected claims by Russia's ambassador that the deadly explosion at Moscow's Balzi Rossi restaurant was meant to intimidate Italians. He said the allegation made no sense because Italy has consistently supported Ukraine.

Zelensky Says Ukraine Will Push to End Russia’s War Before Winter — Zelensky said Ukraine will work to create enough pressure to force Russia toward peace before winter, combining diplomacy, sanctions and medium- and long-range strikes. He cautioned that the timing cannot be guaranteed and accused Putin of preparing to prolong the war.

Wildberries Bans Smartphones at Warehouses After Drone Attacks — Wildberries has prohibited employees from bringing smartphones to its warehouses, allowing only button phones without cameras. The move follows reported filming of drone attacks and air raid alerts at company facilities.

Umerov Appointed as Head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence in Security Reshuffle — Rustem Umerov, the former defense minister and Secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council (RNBO), has been appointed the head of Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SZRU), while former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko was tapped to take his place at the RNBO as part of the government reshuffle that started in July.

Zelensky Orders Ambassadors to Secure Weapons, Advance Europe’s FREYJA Missile Shield — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian ambassadors will advance the Freyja anti-ballistic defense project in Europe and negotiate new drone agreements. He instructed diplomats to prioritize securing weapons and air defense systems for Ukraine.

Drone Falls Near ‘Putin’s Palace’ in Russia, Killing Four People — Four people were killed and 10 wounded when a drone fell on a beach in Arkhipo-Osipovka, about 14 miles from the estate known as “Putin’s Palace.” A Ukrainian Telegram channel claimed the drone was intercepted roughly 300 meters short of a facility linked to a Russian missile producer.

Ihor Klymenko Named Ukraine’s New National Security Council Secretary After Cabinet Shake-Up — Former Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko has been appointed secretary of Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council as President Volodymyr Zelensky continues a sweeping government reshuffle that has seen changes at the defense and interior ministries.

Russia’s Foreign Ministry Calls Moscow Restaurant Bombing ‘Attempt to Intimidate Italians’ — Russia’s Embassy in Italy issued a statement condemning the weekend’s restaurant bombing in Moscow supposedly targeting a Russian general and his associates, claiming that the attack was an attempt to intimidate Italians in Russia because it took place at an Italian restaurant.

Russia Captured More Territory Than Ukraine Reclaimed in July, DeepState Reports — Russian forces captured more Ukrainian territory than Ukraine’s Defense Forces reclaimed in July, the OSINT project DeepState reported. According to the group’s data, Russian forces advanced 36 square kilometers in July, though actual gains may reach 88 square kilometers due to reporting delays. DeepState also noted Ukrainian advances in two additional areas totaling at least 132 square kilometers, however, pendin

Russian Aerospace Forces Commander's Daughter Reportedly Injured in Moscow Blast — Maria Chayko, 25, daughter of Russian Aerospace Forces Commander Aleksandr Chayko, was reportedly among those injured in a Moscow restaurant bombing on Aug. 1, according to Russian outlet Verstka. Her husband, Danylo Peredriy, 27, may have been killed in the blast. The bombing at Balzi Rossi restaurant killed five people and injured 21. Putin’s Continuing War on Ukraine’s Christians — Putin has destroyed 800 churches in Ukraine and killed dozens of pastors and priests. Our five new short films shine a light on stories of faith and courage from the front lines of Ukraine.

WATCH: Ukraine Unleashes FPV-Carrying Magura Sea Drones Against Russian Targets on Land — HUR’s Group 13 used new FPV-carrying Magura maritime platforms to hit a Podlyot radar command vehicle and a Parol-4 friend-or-foe interrogator in occupied Crimea in late July.

Why Russia Does Not Want Peace – Analysis of the Kremlin’s Latest Statements — Despite the desire of senior US officials to bring Ukraine and Russia to the negotiating table, there are still no signs that Russia seeks peace. On the contrary, an analysis of Vladimir Putin and Sergey Lavrov’s statements clearly indicate that Russia is looking for new ways to escalate the conflict.

The War Is Coming Home to Russians — Russia’s war in Ukraine is beginning to directly affect everyday Russians after years of insulation. Is the war coming home to roost? The evidence suggests it is. Rising casualties may force mobilization in Moscow and St. Petersburg, while Ukrainian drone strikes are crippling refineries, logistics networks and major distributors such as Wildberries. With Europe now backing Ukraine at scale, Russia faces economic decline, political strain and a looming eventu

Italy-Led EU Mission Boards Russia-Linked ‘Shadow Fleet’ Tanker in Mediterranean — An Italy-led EU naval mission boarded a sanctioned tanker linked to Russia’s “shadow fleet” in the Mediterranean, the second such operation in under two weeks. The inspection is part of a broader European effort to tighten enforcement of sanctions targeting Moscow’s oil exports.

Baltic Startups Take Aim at Deterring Russia on NATO’s Eastern Flank — Russia’s war in Ukraine has fueled a boom in Baltic defense startups, with companies developing drone and battlefield technologies for Ukraine and NATO allies. Entrepreneurs say the war has accelerated innovation, investment, and military cooperation, strengthening the region’s resilience against growing threats from Russia and Belarus.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Development University, Wildberries Logistics Hub, Crimea in Overnight Raid — Ukrainian drones struck a Russian university reportedly developing drone control systems, a Wildberries logistics hub in Vladimir region, and multiple targets in occupied Crimea overnight, expanding Kyiv’s campaign against Russia’s military and logistics infrastructure.

US to Cede Command of Group Coordinating Military Aid, Training to Ukraine — NATO allies are expected to take over command of the Ukraine Security Assistance Group (SAG-U) as the US scales back its role in Europe. The transition is part of a broader effort to shift responsibility for supporting Ukraine’s military to European partners, while arms deliveries are expected to continue.
